item.subject: maths
item.stem:
The figure shows Sonia's garden plot: rectangle $ABCD$ is $10\ \mathrm{cm}$ by $5\ \mathrm{cm}$, and right triangle $AEB$ has base $10\ \mathrm{cm}$ and height $4\ \mathrm{cm}$ on top of the rectangle.

How should she find the area of the figure?

options.A: Add the rectangle area $10\times 5$ and the triangle area $\dfrac{1}{2}\times 10\times 4$.
options.B: Use only the rectangle area $10\times 5$, because the triangle sits on the rectangle.
options.C: Multiply the rectangle area by the triangle area to get the composite area.
options.D: Any closed garden plot has area $10\times 5$.
